## Read in data, look at it 

```{r}
covariate_data <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar.csv")
# summary(covariate_data)

gene_expression_data <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")

gene_names <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```

## Cleaning data 
```{r}
# clean covariate data to remove labels 
# update data types
# 0 = healthy, 1= asthmatic (should I replace num with char?, maybe down the road)
# batch date is still char, note date
covariate_cleaned <- covariate_data %>% 
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_age_yrs, ".*: ")),
    preg_preeclampsia = str_remove(preg_preeclampsia, ".*: "),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(str_remove(delivery_gestAge_wks, ".*: ")),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(str_remove(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks, ".*: ")),
    batch_Microarray = (str_remove(batch_Microarray, ".*: ")),
    mat_BMI = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_BMI, ".*: ")),
    mat_vitD = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_vitD, ".*: ")),
    mat_asthma = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_asthma, ".*: "))
  )

# head(covariate_cleaned)

# need to make sure geoid is unique before I join the tables below
# the statement is true aka there aren't duplicates so I shouldn't get duplicates
# when I join the tables on geoid

# nrow(covariate_cleaned) == length(unique(covariate_cleaned$geoID))

```



## Pivot gene expression data longer
```{r}
# pivot gene expression data, rename x to probe id for future join
gene_expression_long <- gene_expression_data %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = 2:158,
      names_to = "geoID",
    values_to = "expression_value") %>% 
  rename(PROBEID = X)
# head(gene_expression_long)
```



## Combine data frames
```{r}
# join covariate and expression data on geoid, join gene name on probe id 
pregnancy_data <- gene_expression_long %>% 
  left_join(covariate_cleaned, by = "geoID") %>% 
  left_join(gene_names, by = "PROBEID")

# reorder columns 
pregnancy_data <- pregnancy_data %>% 
  relocate(GENE, .before = "expression_value")

# head(pregnancy_data)

# update preeclampsia and asthma status to be factors
# first check to make sure there are only the two levels I think there are
unique(pregnancy_data$preg_preeclampsia)
unique(pregnancy_data$mat_asthma)

#now mutate to factors
pregnancy_data <- pregnancy_data %>% 
  mutate(
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia,
                               levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia"), labels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
    mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, 
                        levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Healthy", "Asthmatic"))
  )

# do we have any NAs in this data frame?
colSums(is.na(pregnancy_data))

```

data frame looks okay, time to double check
sorted original covariate data and pregnancy_data by geoid and the covariate values for gsm2264363 geoid matched correctly 
searched for gsm2264363 in pregnancy_data and then sorted by probeid, value matched value for gsm2264363 and corresponding probe id (x) in original gene expression data



## Subset selected gene and create the categorical variable 
```{r}
# subset data for selected gene, use pipes to also derive age category, make it a factor!!
# make factor have reference as first level as best practice
shank2_data <- pregnancy_data %>% 
  filter(GENE == "SHANK2") %>%
  mutate(
    mat_age_group = if_else(mat_age_yrs >= 35, "Advanced Age >= 35 Years", "Standard Age <35 Years"),
    mat_age_group = factor(mat_age_group,
                           levels = c("Standard Age <35 Years", "Advanced Age >= 35 Years"), 
                           labels = c("Standard Age <35 Years", "Advanced Age >= 35 Years"))
  )
  
# head(shank2_data)

# calculate sample size for graphs, best practice to exclude NA's 
n_samples <- sum(!is.na(shank2_data$expression_value))

```

## Create plots
```{r}
# colors based on ggthemes solarized 
solar <- c(yellow  = "#b58900", orange = "#cb4b16", red  = "#dc322f",
         magenta = "#d33682", violet = "#6c71c4", blue = "#268bd2",
         cyan    = "#2aa198", green  = "#859900")

#histogram - add line at median
ggplot(shank2_data, aes(x = expression_value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = solar["blue"], color = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(expression_value, na.rm = TRUE)),
               color = solar["orange"], linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(
  title = "Distribution of SHANK2 Gene Expression",
  subtitle =paste0("Dashed line = median; n = ", n_samples),
  x = "SHANK2 Expression",
  y = "Number of Samples") +
  theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0)
    )

# ggsave("SHANK2_Histogram.png", width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

#scatterplot
ggplot(shank2_data, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression_value)) +
  geom_point(color = solar["blue"], alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
              color = solar["red"], fill = solar["orange"], alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "SHANK2 Expression vs. Maternal Vitamin D",
    subtitle = paste0("Line = linear fit with 95% confidence intervals; n = ", n_samples),
    x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)", 
    y = "SHANK2 Expression") +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0)
  )

# ggsave("SHANK2_Scatterplot.png", width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

#boxplot
ggplot(shank2_data, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = expression_value, fill = mat_age_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                             dodge.width  = 0.8,
                                             seed = 33),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.0, color = solar["violet"]) +
  scale_fill_solarized(accent = "blue") +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(
    title    = "SHANK2 Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and Maternal Age",
    subtitle = paste0("Points represent individual samples; n = ", n_samples),
    x        = "Pregnancy Outcome",
    y        = "SHANK2 Expression",
    fill     = "Maternal Age Group"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title.x    = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y    = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10))
  )

# ggsave("SHANK2_Boxplot2.png", width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```

build a function that produces the plots for submission 1 above. Your plots should also incorporate any
feedback from Submission 1.
Your function should take the following inputs:
1. Data frame
2. List of 1 or more gene names
Your function should loop through all genes provided to it to produce the plots from your first
submission (including 1 continuous covariate and 2 categorical covariates).

## Build function
```{r}

# make pretty visuals using artyfarty package
# define palette
# ft_pal <- pal("ft")
fm_pal <- pal("few_medium")


# define list of genes
genes_of_interest <- c("SHANK2", "PRICKLE3", "FIG4")

# define function to create plots for gene list
build_gene_plots <- function(df, list){
  
  # # define list to store plots in 
  # all_hists   <- list()
  # all_scatts  <- list()
  # all_boxps   <- list()
 
   # loop through the genes in the gene list 
  for (gene in list) {
    
    # for selected gene, subset the data and create maternal age categorical variable 
    gene_data <- df %>% 
      filter(GENE == gene) %>%
      mutate(
        mat_age_group = if_else(mat_age_yrs >= 35, "Advanced Age >= 35 Years", "Standard Age <35 Years"),
        mat_age_group = factor(mat_age_group,
                              levels = c("Standard Age <35 Years", "Advanced Age >= 35 Years"), 
                              labels = c("Standard Age <35 Years", "Advanced Age >= 35 Years"))
      )
      
    # calculate sample size for graphs, best practice to exclude NA's
    n_samples <- sum(!is.na(gene_data$expression_value))
    
    # report statistical values on plots 
      # calculate the median for histogram 
      gene_median <- round(median(gene_data$expression_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
      # calculate the correlation for scatterplot
      correlation <- round(cor(gene_data$mat_vitD, gene_data$expression_value), 2)
  
    # build histogram
    gene_hist <- ggplot(gene_data, aes(x = expression_value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = fm_pal[7], color = fm_pal[5], alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(expression_value, na.rm = TRUE)),
                   color = fm_pal[3], linetype = "dashed", linewidth = .8) +
    theme_ft() +
      labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Gene Expression"),
      subtitle =paste0("n = ", n_samples),
      x = paste0(gene, "Expression"),
      y = "Number of Samples") +
      annotate("text", x = gene_median, y = Inf, label = paste("Median:", gene_median), 
               hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, fontface = "italic", size = 4) +
      theme(
          plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10), hjust = 0.5),
          axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
          axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
          plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0)
        )
    
    # build scatterplot 
    gene_scatt <- ggplot(gene_data, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression_value)) +
      geom_point(color = fm_pal[7], alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
                  color = fm_pal[3], fill = fm_pal[5], alpha = 0.3, linewidth = .8) +
      theme_ft() +
      labs(
        title = paste(gene, "Expression vs. Maternal Vitamin D"),
        subtitle = paste0("linear fit with 95% confidence intervals; n = ", n_samples),
        x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)", 
        y = paste0(gene, " Expression")) +
      annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste("r =", correlation), 
               hjust = 2.5, vjust = 1.5, fontface = "italic", size = 4) +
      theme(
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10), hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
        axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
        plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0)
      )
    
    # build boxplot
    gene_boxp <- ggplot(gene_data, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = expression_value, fill = mat_age_group)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7,linewidth = .5,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                                 dodge.width  = 0.8,
                                                 seed = 33),
                 alpha = 0.9, size = 1.0, color = fm_pal[5]) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(fm_pal[7], fm_pal[3])) +
      theme_ft() +
      labs(
        title    = paste(gene,"Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and Maternal Age"),
        subtitle = paste0("n = ", n_samples),
        x        = "Pregnancy Outcome",
        y        = paste(gene, "Expression"),
        fill     = "Maternal Age Group"
      ) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 10), hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title.x    = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
        axis.title.y    = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10))
      )
    
    # # store plots in lists
    # all_hists[[gene]]   <- gene_hist
    # all_scatts[[gene]]  <- gene_scatt
    # all_boxps[[gene]]   <- gene_boxp
    # 
    # # wrap the plot lists
    # combined_hists   <- wrap_plots(all_hists, ncol = 3)
    # combined_scatts  <- wrap_plots(all_scatts, ncol = 3)
    # combined_boxps   <- wrap_plots(all_boxps, ncol = 3) + 
    #                     plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    #                     theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    
    
    # # return individual plots
    print(gene_hist)
    print(gene_scatt)
    print(gene_boxp)
    
    # # save individual plots once
    # ggsave(paste0("S2_", gene, "_Histogram.png"), plot = gene_hist, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)
    # ggsave(paste0("S2_", gene, "_Scatterplot.png"), plot = gene_scatt, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)
    # ggsave(paste0("S2_", gene, "_Boxplot.png"), plot = gene_boxp, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)
    
   
    # # return combined plots
    # print(combined_hists)
    # print(combined_scatts)
    # print(combined_boxps)
    
    # # save combines plots once
    # ggsave("S2_all_Histograms.png", plot = combined_hists, width = 20, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    # ggsave("S2_all_Scatterplots.png", plot = combined_scatts, width = 20, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    # ggsave("S2_all_Boxplots.png", plot = combined_boxps, width = 20, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    
    
  }
}
# run function
  build_gene_plots(pregnancy_data,genes_of_interest)
```
